<!-- Climb batch 29, rung C (rung-numeral-checker): the compiled checker's numerals by P-173, P-174 and P-40: the default where nothing fixes a type, the narrowest default for a type parameter that several numerals fix, the numeral types written only as a parameter's type, a numeral out of range refused statically, a size read as a value a ZZ32; rows 79, 946, 486 and 325 close, 362, 506 and 675 are rewritten, two rows are new. -->

# Rung C: the checker's numerals

- problem: the checker types a numeral `IntLiteral` or `FloatLiteral` by its form and keeps that type wherever nothing converts it (F-57), so `x = 3` is an `IntLiteral` on the compiled path: `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:54`
- spec: P-173 and P-174 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:104`, `:105`); the specification's tie rule, which the default widens: `Specification/basic/inference.tex:299-317`
- precedent: the planner's prototype, step 2 (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-29/probes/literal-default.patch:973-1432`), and the base's numeral reading at a tie (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:459`)
- deviation: no `viaDefault` chain and no trace object (`LiteralDefaults`); a coercion into the default recognised by its form, not marked in a table; the written-only rule allows a parameter's type and names both types; joins, tuples, the range refusal, the unfixed-size fallback and the nat value added: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/CoercionOracle.scala:410`
- historical: `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala`, `impls/Decls.scala`, `impls/Misc.scala`, `CoercionOracle.scala`, `TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`, `STypeChecker.scala`, `staticenv/KindEnv.scala`, `scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala`, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`; the team's tests `Compiled5.ah`, `5.aj`, `5.ak`, `6.az`, `9.g`, `9.j`, `9.p`, `9.t`, `9.u` and `XXX6at.test`, `XXX6bw.test`: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:1`

Java and Scala paths below are under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/`. Line numbers are the tree's at `fa13e6383c`.

## 1. What changed and why

The commits: `7bd7c7dfc7` (the change and its tests), `fe5d146a86` (the `XXX` test of the one fork not built, NEW-C-1), `fa13e6383c` (three revival tests the suite showed broken, respelled). The code of `7bd7c7dfc7` is the final code; the later commits change tests only.

**The default (P-173, fork C1).** A numeral, an `IntLiteralExpr` or `FloatLiteralExpr` node as written or as the fold made it, where nothing fixes a type converts into its default: `ZZ32`, or `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, `RR64` with a radix point. The default applies to a numeral node, never to an expression of a numeral type, so `t = x` inside `coerce(x: IntLiteral)` stays an `IntLiteral`. The sites:

- an untyped binding, top level and local, one variable or several (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Decls.scala:252`, `:289`, `:343`, `:384`), through `defaultNumeral` (`impls/Functionals.scala:1016`): a numeral alone; each element of a tuple on its own; the branches of an `if` with `else`, a `case`, a block's last expression or a one-block `do`, when every result is a numeral, together into the narrowest default holding them all (`joinNumerals`, `joinInto`, `:1030`, `:1046`);
- a parameter or a typed place whose type holds the numeral without conversion and fixes no type, `Any`, `Object`, `Number`, where the default fits too (`defaultAtUnfixed`, `:1078`): in `checkApplicableWithoutInference` (`:490`), its `Any`-domain branch (`:512`), after the subtyping inference (`:279`), in the coercion attempt (`:410`), and at every typed binding, assignment, field and return through `STypeChecker.checkExpr` (`scala_src/typechecker/STypeChecker.scala:506`);
- a parameter or typed place whose type declares no coercion from the numeral's type but holds its default, as `Index` holds `ZZ32` (`defaultFits`, `:1093`; `STypeChecker.scala:510`, `Functionals.scala:411`, `:491`);
- a type parameter that numerals alone fix, with no expected type: before the subtyping inference (`preDefault`, `:1121`, called at `:198`), and as the coercion attempt's one choice for that parameter (`:385`), the narrowest default holding every value (`numeralDefault`, `:998`), with the attempt's ordinary choices as a fallback where the default finds no candidate (`:417-423`);
- a dotted receiver written as a numeral, where the default type has the member (`defaultReceiver`, `:1105`; called at `:1360` and `impls/Misc.scala:347`), the prototype's receiver rule, so the prelude's `(1).asNN32` keeps its numeral.

It does not apply: at a parameter of a numeral's own type (`isNumeralType`, `:989`), which a coercion's or an operator's parameter is; at a place whose type declares a coercion from the numeral's type (the eight number types on the one library, the prelude's six, a program's type with `coerce(x: IntLiteral)`), where that coercion runs; at a type parameter that a non-numeral argument also fixes, or another parameter type mentions, or the expected type fixes, which the inference sets as before (P-74); to a join with a non-numeral branch; to an `if` without `else`.

**The ranking (fork C4, the prototype's step 5 in its narrow form).** A numeral's coercion into its own default ranks as no coercion wherever it is built: `NumeralConversion.isDefault` and `counts` (`scala_src/typechecker/CoercionOracle.scala:432`, `:439`), read by `counted` (`impls/Functionals.scala:742`) and by `moreSpecificCandidate` (`scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1147-1148`). It is read from the coercion's form, a `TraitCoercionInvocation` of a numeral node into the library type of its default's name, not from a table of marked nodes, so it holds for every copy of the node and keeps no state. Before the subtyping inference a numeral at a parameter of exactly its default type takes that coercion (`preDefault`), so `ee[\nat n\](x: ZZ32)` fits `ee(5)` as it is. So `gg(5, w)` runs `gg[\T extends Number\](x: ZZ32, y: T)` and the narrower declaration is the checker's static choice, P-173's reading of P-49 (fork C8).

**The narrowest default (fork C1, P-173).** `pick(3, 3000000000)` is `pick[\ZZ64\]` on the prelude (`LiteralDefaultCompiled`); on the one library, read by the count stage's driver, `<|3000000000, 0.5|>` is a `List[\RR64\]` (section 4).

**The written-only rule (P-174, fork C2).** `TypeWellFormedChecker` refuses `IntLiteral` or `FloatLiteral` written in a program's file anywhere but as the whole type of a parameter of a function, method, coercion, operator or function expression: "IntLiteral cannot be written in a program except as a parameter's type." (`scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:293`). An object's value parameter is a field, and is refused. Files under `Library/` and `LibraryBuiltin/` are exempt. A type that the checker infers from such a parameter keeps the parameter type's span and is not refused: the rule reads written types (`parameterTypeSpans`, `:48`; `numeralTypeWritten`, `:67`). The names are read from `Types.INT_LITERAL` and `Types.FLOAT_LITERAL`, so N's switch of the names by library carries the rule to `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral`.

**No chain (fork C4).** `buildCoercion` returns the coercion it checks (`CoercionOracle.scala:171`), without the prototype's `viaDefault`: `c: CC64 = 3` for a `CC64` with only `coerce(x: ZZ32)` is refused, "Right-hand side has type IntLiteral, but declared type is CC64." (`XXXLiteralNoCoercionRefused`). `defaultFits` does not chain either: it takes the default only where the default is a subtype of the place's type.

**The range refusal (fork C3, row 325).** `NumeralConversion.outOfRange` (`CoercionOracle.scala:459`): an integer numeral outside `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` or `NN64`, and an integer or float numeral whose one rounding into `RR64` or `RR32` is an infinity, has no coercion into that library type (`:172`). At a typed place the checker signals "The numeral 4294967295 is out of range for ZZ32, whose values are -2147483648 to 2147483647." or "The numeral … rounds to infinity in RR64." at the numeral (`STypeChecker.scala:513`); at a call that no candidate fits, each such numeral against each candidate's parameter type, beside the call's own error (`signalNumeralRanges`, `impls/Functionals.scala:1169`, called at `:795`). At an overloaded call, a candidate whose parameter cannot hold the numeral is not applicable, so `z MAX 3000000000` for a `ZZ32` `z` runs `ZZ64`'s `MAX` (`NumeralBeyondWidthMax`, promoted).

**The size read as a value (P-40, fork C5, row 486).** `KindEnv.getType` answers `ZZ32` for a `nat` or `int` parameter (`scala_src/typechecker/staticenv/KindEnv.scala:71-72`), the prelude's `CompilerBuiltin.ZZ32` or the one library's `FortressLibrary.ZZ32` (`sizeValueType`, `:112`); the code generator reads such a value where its type is `ZZ32` and converts the class loader's `IntLiteral` constant by `asZZ32` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:6342-6364`). So `u: NN32 = n` is refused, "Right-hand side has type ZZ32, but declared type is NN32.", and `v = n` is a `ZZ32`.

**A size the default leaves unknown.** A declaration that only the default at a parameter of its default type makes applicable, and whose size the call then leaves unknown, is checked as the numeral is, without the default (`impls/Functionals.scala:288-292`), so `ee(5)` is not refused by P-40's rule for an unfixed size: section 9, decision 6.

**A static argument of a numeral's own type.** A subtyping inference that a numeral argument fixes at the numeral's own type is left to the attempt with coercion, which reads the numeral by its default (`:172`), where no argument is a function expression still unchecked; `Compiled5.bu`'s `gapply(fn (x) => x + 1, 5)` needed that condition (section 3).

## 9. Decisions

1. **The default recognised by the coercion's form.** A `TraitCoercionInvocation` of a numeral node into the library type named by its default ranks as no coercion (`NumeralConversion.isDefault`). Ways not taken: the prototype's identity table `LiteralDefaults` (`literal-default.patch:1137-1166`), which keeps every marked node for the JVM's life and misses a copied node; a flag on the node, which the AST does not carry. Evidence: the ranking reads the node it is handed (`STypesUtil.scala:1147`).
2. **The written-only rule allows a parameter's whole type, and nothing else.** Ways not taken: the prototype's refusal everywhere ("cannot be written in a program: a numeral has its own type only while the checker types the program"), which P-174's coercions from the numeral types contradict; the rule over inferred types too, which fork C2 declines; a parameter's type anywhere inside, as `Maybe[\IntLiteral\]`, which writes a static argument. An object's value parameter counts as a field. Evidence: fork C2; P-174.
3. **The default where a place's type has no coercion from the numeral's type but holds its default (`defaultFits`)**, so `fi(3)` passes at `Index` and a float numeral at the prelude's `Number`. Way not taken: the default only at `Any`, `Object` and `Number`, the prototype's. Evidence: the judgement's repair 1, "every other type, and no type, takes the default" (`reviews/literal-design-judgement-2026-11-08.md`, section 1), which P-173's text follows.
4. **Joins and tuples at an untyped binding**, through the result positions, and the join's numerals at their narrowest default together. Ways not taken: the prototype's coercion of the whole join, whose branches keep literal values; a join's branches each at its own default, which the judgement's repair 4 declines. Evidence: fork C1.
5. **The range refusal as "no coercion", with the message at typed places and beside a call that no candidate fits.** Ways not taken: a coercion built and an error signalled, which would make an overloaded call refuse `z MAX 3000000000` instead of choosing `ZZ64`'s; the message only at typed places. Evidence: fork C3; `NumeralBeyondWidthMax`'s assertion, "a numeral converts only into a type that holds its value".
6. **A size left unknown after the default is checked without the default.** `ee[\nat n\](x: ZZ32)` fits `ee(5)` as it is by fork C4, but leaves `n` unknown, and P-40 refuses a call whose chosen declaration has a size it cannot fix. The checker so checks the declaration without the default, by subtyping, where it does not apply: `ee(x: Any)` is the static choice, the default makes the argument a `ZZ32`, and the compiled dispatch, which tests run-time types, runs `ee[\nat n\]`, so `ee(5)` gives 1 (`LiteralDefaultCompiled`, `InferO2Pos`). Ways not taken: the static choice of `ee[\nat n\]`, refused by P-40's rule ("Could not infer static argument nat n without context.", the first build of the change); the default not ranked as no coercion at a generic's parameter, which would leave `gg(5, w)` at the plain declaration. No decision of the curator covers the case where P-40 and fork C4 meet; a question below.
7. **The written-only message**: "IntLiteral cannot be written in a program except as a parameter's type." Way not taken: the prototype's text, now false. Evidence: fork C2, "renamed for both names".
8. **C6 not built** (NEW-C-1). The integer literal fold makes `-3` one node before the checker and keeps no reference to the prefix operator, so the checker cannot apply the program's `-` without a reference the disambiguator makes (`compiler/desugarer/IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java:148-153`). Ways not taken: a fresh operator reference built in the checker, which the disambiguator's binding of operators does not reach; refusing a negative numeral at every program's type, which would refuse `c: CC64 = -3` where the type declares `-` too. Until the switch-over the prelude's `IntLiteral` carries the sign, so the coercion reads -3 exactly.
9. **The tests' respellings**: the prototype's `Boolean` arm; the team tests at `ZZ32`, the type their comments name; the nat tests read through types where a value cannot hold the size.
10. **No speed pass**: the profile shows the change in under 0.3 % of the samples.

Conditions: the compiled checker, on the prelude and on the one library at the base. Meaning: rows 79 and 946 close; an expression of a numeral's type keeps it.
2. **A numeral's conversion into its own default ranks as no coercion wherever it is built**, read from the coercion's form (`scala_src/typechecker/CoercionOracle.scala:432-439`, `impls/Functionals.scala:742`, `scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1147-1148`). So `gg(5, w)` runs `gg[\T extends Number\](x: ZZ32, y: T)` statically (`compiler_tests/InferO2Pos`). Where only that default makes a generic declaration applicable and its size stays unknown, as `ee[\nat n\](x: ZZ32)` at `ee(5)`, the declaration is checked without the default (`impls/Functionals.scala:288-292`): the static choice is `ee(x: Any)` and the compiled dispatch runs the `ZZ32` declaration, 1. 3. **IntLiteral and FloatLiteral are written in a program only as the whole type of a parameter** of a function, method, coercion, operator or function expression; elsewhere, an object's value parameter included, "IntLiteral cannot be written in a program except as a parameter's type." (`scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:293`). Files under `Library/` and `LibraryBuiltin/` are exempt; a type inferred from such a parameter is not refused. 4. **A program's type with no coercion from the numeral's type refuses a numeral**: no chain through the default (`CoercionOracle.scala:171`). Meaning: row 486 closes; a size of 2^31 or more cannot be read as a value (NEW-C-2), and `NatRtBigSize` and `NatArithBeyondRun` now read such sizes through types.

**The compiled checker converts a numeral where nothing fixes a type into its default, refuses one out of range, and refuses a numeral type written other than as a parameter's type.** Where no place's type has a coercion from the numeral's type or is a numeral type, a numeral becomes a `ZZ32`, or a `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, or an `RR64` with a radix point; a type parameter that numerals alone fix takes the narrowest default holding them all; the conversion into the default ranks as no coercion; a numeral outside a bounded number type's range, or rounding to an infinity, is a static error; `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` are written in a program only as a parameter's type; a `nat` or `int` parameter read as a value is a `ZZ32`. result.reportText:
# Rung N, rung-numeral-types: the numeral types NaturalNumeral and RadixPointNumeral below Numeral, each number type's coercions and = pairs, the 24 glue bindings gone, and walk's numerals converted where they stand

- problem: walk keeps a float numeral at `RR64` a `FloatLiteral` (row 943, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:635`), `QQ` takes no float numeral (row 944, `:636`), `NN32`, `NN64` and `RR32` refuse numerals (row 454, `:610`), `RR64` refuses 3000000000 (row 443, `:609`), `u + 1` at `NN32` is a `ZZ64` (row 484, `:156`), `round(2.5_10)` throws (row 361, `:602`), and `IntLiteral`'s own arithmetic answers a `ZZ32` (row 578, `:620`)
- spec: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-148` (numerals have their own types, which libraries convert by coercions) and `:83-129` (the four numbers); `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:145-153`
- precedent: `value object Ratio(num: ZZ, den: ZZ) extends { QQ }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:648` at the base), the prototype's library step (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-29/probes/literal-default.patch:1-400`), and `Types.CHARACTER`'s switch by library (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Types.java:78-91` at the base)
- deviation: walk converts a numeral into the eight number types through the library's own coercion, called once per site and type, not by a Java conversion per type (fork N7) (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Coercions.java:88-115`); `RR32`'s rounding binding sits in `FortressBuiltin`, beside `RR32`, and `RR64`'s and the numerals' in `FortressLibrary` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:208-210`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:668-670`); `strToFloat` gains a `ZZ32` base, a line beyond the declarations the brief names (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4839-4840`)
- historical: `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, `Library/Constants.fsi`, `Library/Constants.fss`, `Library/ReflectiveQuickCheck.fss`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `compiler/Types.java`, `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala`, `nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java`, `interpreter/env/LazilyEvaluatedCell.java`, `interpreter/evaluator/{BaseEnv,Evaluator,EvaluatorBase,Init,LHSEvaluator}.java`, `interpreter/evaluator/values/{FBigNum,FFloat,FInt,FLong,FOrdinaryObject,FunctionClosure,GenericFunctionOrConstructor,MethodClosure,NonPrimitive,OverloadedFunction,OverloadedMethod}.java` (under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/`), and the team's tests `ProjectFortress/tests/NumberPrintTest.fss`, `sequivTest.fss`, `XXXextendIntLiteral.fss`, `XXXextendFloatLiteral.fss`

Commits on `wip/rung-numeral-types`: `f7b46ce742` (the tests, before any edit), `9e259096a9` (the library, walk and the checker), `d541ae9682` (the test changes and walk's inference hook), `e3adeedb64` (`strToFloat`'s base and the XXX test of an undefined `typecase` arm). Every stage and suite named below ran on the commit it names.

## What changed and why

**The library.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:454-494` and `.fss:668-721` declare, beside `Ratio`, `trait Numeral extends Number comprises { NaturalNumeral, RadixPointNumeral }` with the four getters abstract (`digits`, `fractionDigits` and `radix` at `ZZ32`, `digitValue` at `ZZ`), and the value objects `NaturalNumeral(digits: ZZ32, radix: ZZ32, digitValue: ZZ)`, whose `fractionDigits` is 0, and `RadixPointNumeral(digits: ZZ32, fractionDigits: ZZ32, radix: ZZ32, digitValue: ZZ)`. Each has `asString`, the numeral as the Working Draft writes one (its digits in its radix, at least `digits` of them, upper case, the radix point after `digits - fractionDigits` of them, `_r` where the radix is not ten), `asFloat(self): RR64` by one rounding, and its reversed `=` pairs: `NaturalNumeral` at the eight number types, `RadixPointNumeral` at `RR64`, `QQ` and `RR32`, each `do c: T = self; (c = b) end` as the library writes its pairs (`.fss:418` at the base). The number types' coercions, renamed or new, each with its pair:

| type | coercions from the numeral types, and their bodies | pair |
|---|---|---|
| `RR64` | `coerce(x: NaturalNumeral) = asFloat(x)`, `coerce(x: RadixPointNumeral) = asFloat(x)` (`.fss:389-390`) | both (`.fss:419-420`) |
| `QQ` | `Ratio(x.digitValue, 1)`; `x.digitValue / r^(x.fractionDigits)` for `r: ZZ = big(x.radix)`, reduced by `ZZ`'s `/` (`.fss:565-569`) | both (`.fss:588-589`) |
| `AnyIntegral` | `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by the value, which is never negative (`.fss:723-728`) | none, as at the base |
| `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN64`, `ZZ` | `x.digitValue.asZZ32`, `.asZZ64`, `.asNN64`, `x.digitValue` (`.fss:829`, `:935`, `:1045`, `:1155`) | `NaturalNumeral` (`:845`, `:956`, `:1064`, `:1175`) |
| `NN32` | `x.digitValue.asNN32` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:430`) | `NaturalNumeral` (`:453`) |
| `RR32` | `numeralRR32(x.digitValue, x.radix, 0)` and `numeralRR32(x.digitValue, x.radix, x.fractionDigits)` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:214-215`) | both, new (`:258-259`) |

`RR64` comprises `{ Float }` (`.fsi:294`); `Float`'s `asFloat(self): RR64` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:82`); the `^` over the numeral in `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN64`, `ZZ` and `NN32` renamed, its body `self^(b.digitValue.asZZ32)`; `pi` and `e` at `RR64` (`Library/Constants.fsi:16-17`, `.fss:15-16`); `ReflectiveQuickCheck.fss:40` chooses `theType[\ZZ32\]()` where it chose `IntLiteral`, and the arm `theType[\IntLiteral\]() => Just[\AnyGen\](genZZ32)` (`:157` at the base), which repeated the `ZZ32` arm above it, is dropped. `value object IntLiteral` and `value object FloatLiteral` leave `FortressBuiltin.fsi` and `.fss` with their 24 glue bindings; no line of the one library names either now. The glue classes `interpreter/glue/prim/IntLiteral.java` and `FloatLiteral.java`, and walk's `FIntLiteral` and `FFloatLiteral`, stay in the tree, unused (fork N11).

**The helper pair** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:264-307`): `public static double numeralToDouble(BigInteger v, int r, int m)` and `public static float numeralToFloat(BigInteger v, int r, int m)`, the value `v / r^m` rounded once to the nearest double or float, ties to even, subnormals included, by an integer quotient at the format's last significand bit and its remainder; two private helpers (`lsbExponent`, `roundedQuotient`) whose types all map to Fortress, as the wrapper generator needs. The bindings: `private numeralRR64(v: ZZ, r: ZZ32, m: ZZ32): RR64` in `FortressLibrary.fss:668-670`, which both numerals' `asFloat` call, and `private numeralRR32(v: ZZ, r: ZZ32, m: ZZ32): RR32` in `FortressBuiltin.fss:208-210`, which `RR32`'s coercions call; walk carries `ZZ` in `BigInteger`, `ZZ32` in `int`, `RR64` in `double` and `RR32` in `float` (F-299). Walk's default for a radix-point numeral calls `numeralToDouble` in Java (`Numerals.java`), so the default and `RR64`'s coercion round alike.

**Walk's numerals** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/Numerals.java`, new). `Evaluator.forIntLiteralExpr` and `forFloatLiteralExpr` (`Evaluator.java:1632`, `:1636`) return the value of the numeral's site, made once: its default, a subclass of `FInt`, `FLong`, `FBigNum` or `FFloat` (their constructors opened to the package) that carries a `Site` with the four numbers. The digits as written come from the numeral's text, since the node keeps the value and not the trailing zeros (`3.14150` has `digitValue` 314150, `fractionDigits` 5). The places:

- a typed binding, a field and an assignment (`LHSEvaluator.java:115`, `:220-230`, `BaseEnv.java:332`, `LazilyEvaluatedCell.java:69`), a parameter (`NonPrimitive.java:247`, `:272`), and a declared return type (`FunctionClosure.java:212-221`, `MethodClosure.java:85-89`, `Numerals.atReturn`): where the default does not fit the type, `Coercions.coerce` makes a numeral the numeral object at a numeral type, else converts it through the place type's coercion whose parameter type is the narrowest holding the numeral type, with no chain through the default (`Coercions.java:59`, `:88-115`, `:268`); the result is kept for the site and type (`Numerals.converted`), so a site gives one object of a reference type; a store keeps the default alone (`Numerals.plain`, deep for tuples);
- an integer numeral outside an integer type's range is not converted, so the place refuses it as walk refused one at a binding before: 'Type mismatch binding 3000000000' (`Numerals.inRange`);
- dispatch (`OverloadedFunction.java:2278-2342`, `:2712`): a declaration fits a numeral as it is where its parameter is the numeral's own type or admits its default; of those, the one that the defaults alone fit, unless the own-type fit's domain lies strictly below it; with no fit, the coercion attempt, each numeral converting only from its own type; and a tie among those, an ambiguous coercion, reads each numeral at its default; a functional method chosen at a numeral's own type receives the numeral object before walk finds the method on it (`Coercions.withNumeralObjects`). The three dispatch caches key a numeral apart from a value of its default type (`Numerals.keys`; `OverloadedFunction.java:99`, `OverloadedMethod.java:29`, `GenericFunctionOrConstructor.java:24`);
- the head of `EvaluatorBase.inferAndInstantiateGenericFunction` (`EvaluatorBase.java:90`): the inference reads each numeral at its default, and where the numerals at one type parameter's positions include a radix point, one beyond `ZZ32` by a `ZZ32` stand-in, so that walk's promotion gives `RR64`; the call's numerals then convert at the instance;
- `SEQV` (`FOrdinaryObject.java:48-49`): two numeral objects compare by `digitValue / radix^fractionDigits`, reduced, across both numeral types;
- `Init.java:46` empties the sites between runs.

**The checker.** `Types.INT_LITERAL` and `FLOAT_LITERAL` are no longer final and switch with the libraries, as `CHARACTER` does: the prelude's `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` under the compiler's, `FortressLibrary`'s `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral` under the one library (`Types.java:61-62`, `:75-95`). `Functionals.isNumeral` counts a numeral with a radix point, and `numeralReading` reads one as `RR64` (`Functionals.scala:418-444`), the prototype's tie rule, written inside the two functions and with no new function, since rung C adds functions near them.

**`strToFloat`** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4839-4840`): its `10^k` and `10^(|frac|)` became `ten^k` for `ten: ZZ32 = 10`. Without it the count stage found two errors there ("The stages").

The count, on `e3adeedb64`, timed (P-148, the float tie rule being checking code), on nproc 4, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 2100 MHz, load at start 0.97 3.12 4.73, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`:

## The ladder

## Revival change

**The change.** The Working Draft of February 2011 gives a numeral the types `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,10,v\]`, their explicit-radix variants, `Literal[\v\]` and `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, whose static arguments are the digit count, the digits after the radix point, the radix and the value, and says that "Numerals are not directly converted to any of the number types because, as in common mathematical usage, we expect them to be polymorphic" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-141`); it says nothing of whether two string literals of one text are one object, and that a `nat` parameter "may ... appear in any context that a variable of type NN32 can appear" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/trait-parameters.tex:83-86`). The revised specification says that every numeral is a `Numeral`, a `NaturalNumeral` or a `RadixPointNumeral` with no static parameters, its four numbers fields of its value; that a numeral converts where it stands, into the type its place fixes (a type with a coercion from the numeral type, or a numeral type), exactly into the integer types and `QQ` and with one rounding into `RR64` and `RR32`, out of range a static error, and elsewhere into `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, or `RR64` with a radix point; that an expression of numerals alone folds exactly into a signed constant with those defaults and `QQ` for a quotient; that a program's type receives a numeral only through its own coercion, once per place; that a numeral type is written only as a parameter type; that a `nat` used as a value is a `ZZ32`; and that two string literals of one text are one object, a concatenation of literals folded into one (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:72-235`; `constant.tex:80-133`; `inference.tex:305-350`; `trait-parameters.tex:105-113`; `objects.tex:66-74`). No test: an edit of the specification has none; the specification's build checks it, and the rungs' tests show the behaviour on the merged tree. The reason, as evidence: the Working Draft gives numerals types of their own so that "library designers [can] decide how numerals should interact with other types of objects by defining coercion operations" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:141-145`), which the team built under the names `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` with the exact value at the coercion ("ZZ32 now coerces IntLiteral as described in the spec", commit `128f313b5b`, 2009) but never with the four numbers; a coercion handed a double rounds twice where one rounding from the exact value gives the nearest value; and every team source that speaks of literals makes equal literals one value ("Literals are values; they do not require evaluation", `literals.tex:25-26`; "All literals represent value objects", `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/literals.tick:29`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_regressions/seqv.fss:22`).

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The fold is the compiler's phase INTEGERLITERALFOLDING (`compiler/IntegerLiteralfolder.java`, `compiler/phases/IntegerLiteralFoldingPhase.java`), a desugaring before the checker that walk now runs too (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md`, B.5: the desugaring phases are shared, Shell's switches choose the visitors). Walk evaluates the folded tree as it is; walk's evaluator is not edited. The typed-place constant is the coercion desugarer's, which only the compiled path runs (`references/interpreter.md`, "Where a fix of walk belongs": walk turns off coercion desugaring), and the code generator's literal methods. The once-per-site call is the code generator's.
Precedents counted: the team's fold has one result form for integers, `ExprFactory.makeIntLiteralExpr(info, value)`, used at 12 places in `foldBinaryOperator` and 3 in `forOpExprOnly` at b430f9f428; the new fold keeps it for integers. The code generator keeps a value computed once in a static field set by a static initializer in three ways: the component class's caching tables (`CodeGen.java:1926-1986` at the base), the trait and object classes' `initializedStaticFields_TO` (`:4821-4845`, three registrations at `:2629`, `:4575`, `:4773`), and a top-level variable's singleton class, set when that class loads at its first use (`:6242-6275`). The new sites follow the first, in the component class. The library's own way does not apply: no library source is edited.

Ways the language and the code offer, and the one chosen (decisions below):
- the folded negative radix-point result: a negative numeral node, prefix minus built from the infix minus's reference, prefix minus reused from the component (chosen);
- the once-per-site call: in the class that holds the site, in a lazy holder class per site, in the component class (chosen);
- the raising coercion's test: an `XXX` name on a designed failure, a JUnit test compiling a program, a harness key (chosen).

**The change.**
- The team's compiled path folds integer numerals before the checker, and walk folds nothing (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/PhaseOrder.java:125-147` at b430f9f428: the fold is in `compilerPhaseOrder` only). So under walk `2147483647 + 1` is 2147483648 and `0.1 + 0.2` is `0.3`. The reason: the Working Draft's static expressions of literals and operators denote exact values, and a static rational expression in a floating-point computation incurs at most one rounding (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:163-173`; `constant.tex`, "Static Expressions"); measured: the team's fold stops the compile at `3 CHOOSE 5` ("Integer Literal folding: Need to do something for factorial of negative values") and makes `a: ZZ32 = 2147483647 BOXPLUS 1` die with "Not in range for ZZ32: 2147483648".

The reason: the Draft's one rounding (above).
- The team's compiled program calls its own coercion from a numeral at each evaluation of the numeral's site, so one site gave distinct reference objects (a probe on the base: `start`, `coerce  3`, `coerce  3`, `coerce  4`, `a SEQV b  false`). The tree calls it once per site, when the component's class is initialized, and every evaluation reads the one result; a coercion that raises stops the program before `run()` (tests `NumeralCoercionOnceCompiled`, `NumeralCoercionRaisesCompiled`). The reason: a numeral is one constant of the program text, and each construction of a reference object is a new object (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:51-53`), so a call at each evaluation made one written numeral many objects.
